coverage_notes:
Consolidated 4-angle pool to 86 candidates → 84 final after dedup (no near-dup pages remain). Removed: the duplicate ExRx Directory entry (https://exrx.net/Lists/Directory appeared twice — kept one canonical id exercise-movements-exrx-directory). All other pool entries are distinct pages and were retained. Two PowerliftingTechnique grip articles (mixed-grip-deadlift, straps-vs-hooks) from the pool are NOT in this final set — they were judged redundant against the StrengthMath, Torokhtiy (x2) and Starting Strength grip-tool coverage and dropped to avoid practitioner-blog over-weighting; the strap/hook/grip decision is already covered by one T2 (Starting Strength), the IJSPP T2 review, four T1 strap studies, and two Torokhtiy T3 guides. Wait — to be precise, I retained the strongest of each grip angle and dropped only the two PowerliftingTechnique pages and did not invent replacements.

TIER recalibration applied per grading rules: systematic reviews → T0 (Neto GMax, Martin-Fuentes deadlift EMG, Kassiano varying-exercises); primary EMG / RCT / moment-arm model → T1 (PeerJ model, Sperandei & grip-variation lat EMG, Contreras squat-vs-hipthrust, RDL-variant EMG, bench-incline EMG, Chaves & repatterning pec trials, non-uniform pec, varying-exercises trial, all four strap studies, pull-up grip study); expert consensus → T2 (all RP/Israetel guides, SBS/Nuckols guides, Henselmans x2, Starting Strength, IJSPP strap review, GMax clinical commentary); mechanistic/practitioner/databases → T3 (Beardsley Medium x6, Nippard x2, ExRx pages, weighttraining.guide, StrengthLog, MuscleWiki, free-exercise-db, wger, M&S, ISSA, N1, Muscle PhD, Torokhtiy, StrengthMath, Contreras blog).

LICENSE recalibration: PMC/PeerJ open-access → redistribute-ok (CC). Public-domain/open datasets (free-exercise-db Unlicense, exercemus MIT, wger AGPL) → redistribute-ok. PubMed-abstract-only and publisher-paywalled journals (Human Kinetics JAB/IJSPP, ScienceDirect/Elsevier, JSCR, Sports Biomechanics/ResearchGate) → reference-only. PMC11367169 / PMC7449336 etc. confirmed PMC-hosted → redistribute-ok. One PubMed record (non-uniform pec excitation, 34644424) full-text OA status not confirmable from the abstract page → license_note=unknown per default. PARSER: github-md for the four raw-GitHub markdown/JSON URLs (free-exercise-db json+repo, exercemus json, wger repo); trafilatura for every HTML page including all PMC/PubMed/ScienceDirect/ResearchGate article pages (no 'pubmed' parser exists — trafilatura on the article HTML).

NAMED-AUTHORITY coverage check (from PLAN): ExRx.net ✓ (directory + class-analyses + glossary + 4 category lists + 3 kinesiology analyses); Stronger By Science/Nuckols ✓ (8 pages incl. exercise-selection, regional-hypertrophy, compound, stretch, leg-extension, squat, deadlift, grip); Renaissance Periodization/Israetel ✓ (15 RP guides — master + per-muscle + forearm-demystified); Chris Beardsley ✓ (6 Medium mechanism notes + the PeerJ moment-arm model); Jeff Nippard ✓ (push + pull); Menno Henselmans ✓ (exercise-selection + lat-prayers); PubMed/PMC EMG & moment-arm ✓ (12 studies covering the disputes the PLAN names: lat row-vs-pulldown, hip-thrust-vs-squat glute bias, RDL hamstring bias, incline-vs-flat pec heads, grip-bypass/straps).

DROPPED authority — MASS Research Review: named in the PLAN's source categories but NO fetchable MASS URL surfaced in any discovery angle (MASS is a fully paywalled subscription PDF review with no public per-article pages), so it cannot be a canonical directly-fetchable source row. Its function (synthesis of the EMG/regional-bias literature) is fully substituted by the T0 systematic reviews (Neto, Martin-Fuentes, Kassiano) and the SBS regional-hypertrophy/exercise-selection pages, which cover the same evidence with redistributable or fetchable text. Flagged here so a later session can add a specific MASS article URL if one becomes accessible.

EQUIPMENT-CLASS coverage (all six classes required by PLAN): barbell/dumbbell/cable/machine/smith/bodyweight movers are all carried by the structured databases (free-exercise-db, exercemus, wger, ExRx directory, M&S, MuscleWiki). Machine→free-weight/cable substitution specifically: ISSA machine-alternatives, N1 free-weights-vs-cables, SBS exercise-selection, Muscle PhD variation, ExRx class-analyses schema. Grip-bypass family (straps/hooks/cuffs/chest-supported) for the left-pinky constraint: SBS grip, RP forearm guides x2, Starting Strength, IJSPP review, StrengthMath, Torokhtiy x2, plus four T1 strap studies + pull-up grip study. PATTERN coverage: push/pull/hinge/squat/lunge/plantarflexion/elbow-flexion/core all hit by StrengthLog four-movements, weighttraining.guide pattern pages, ExRx kinesiology analyses + category lists, and the per-muscle RP guides. Final count 84 sources — above the 28–50 target band; recommend a downstream trim if a tighter set is wanted, but every row is a distinct directly-fetchable page and no padding/invented URLs are present (all URLs originate from the supplied pool, which came from prior WebSearch/fetch results). T0/T1/T2 make up 36 of 84; T3 (40+) is database/mechanistic-explainer heavy because mover attribution for a 120–200-exercise library legitimately needs the broad structured databases and per-pattern explainers.

sources.title: free-exercise-db (yuhonas) — exercises.json (800+ exercises, public domain)
sources.notes: Public-domain (Unlicense) structured JSON of 800+ exercises with primaryMuscles, secondaryMuscles, equipment, force (push/pull), mechanic (isolation/compound), category, instructions. Best directly-fetchable redistributable spine for prime/secondary movers + equipment + force vector across all six equipment classes.

sources.title: free-exercise-db — repo README & schema (Unlicense)
sources.notes: Documents the JSON schema (force, mechanic, category, primary/secondary muscles, equipment, level) and confirms Unlicense/public-domain. Field-interpretation reference for the exercises.json dataset.

sources.title: exercemus/exercises — minified-exercises.json (curated open-license set)
sources.notes: MIT-coded, open-license-curated dataset (merges exercemus, wger.de, exercises.json) with equipment, primary_muscles, secondary_muscles, category, tempo, and per-exercise license metadata. Cross-check / supplement to free-exercise-db.

sources.title: wger — self-hosted FLOSS fitness/workout database (AGPL-3.0)
sources.notes: Open-source (AGPL) exercise wiki: 845+ exercises by category, 16 muscle groups, 12 equipment types, primary & secondary targets. Fixture data + self-hostable DB; redistributable open movement reference.

sources.title: wger REST API documentation (open exercise database)
sources.notes: Public zero-auth REST API (wger.de/api/v2/) exposing exercises with muscles, equipment, categories, images. Programmatic access path to the wger open database.

sources.title: MuscleWiki — interactive exercise library / muscle map
sources.notes: 2000+ exercises filterable by force type (push/pull/static), muscle group, equipment, mechanics (isolation/compound), grip; interactive muscle-map linking target muscle to exercises. Per-exercise target-muscle + force-vector cross-check. Proprietary.

sources.title: MuscleWiki API documentation
sources.notes: API metadata schema for 1900+ MuscleWiki exercises: target body parts, force, mechanics, equipment, demo media. Documents the structured per-exercise fields. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Exercise Directory (2100+ exercises by muscle)
sources.notes: Master directory indexing 2100+ exercises by muscle/body-part/apparatus; entry point to per-exercise prime-mover/synergist/stabilizer analyses and the canonical lookup for same-muscle substitution. Dedup: appeared twice in pool, kept once. Proprietary — read for facts.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Exercise Classifications and Analyses
sources.notes: Defines ExRx's Basic/Auxiliary, Mechanics (compound/isolated), and Force (push/pull) classification system — the schema behind force_vector, is_compound, and machine-to-free-weight substitution mapping. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Kinesiology Glossary (muscle role definitions)
sources.notes: Definitions of functional muscle roles (prime mover/agonist, synergist, dynamic stabilizer, stabilizer, antagonist stabilizer) — the mover-attribution taxonomy underpinning prime vs secondary classification across the library. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Chest (weight) Exercises list
sources.notes: Horizontal-push category list (presses, flyes) linking to per-exercise prime-mover/stabilizer analyses. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Back (weight) Exercises list
sources.notes: Horizontal/vertical-pull category list (rows, pulldowns, pull-ups) linking to prime-mover/synergist/stabilizer breakdowns. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Shoulder (weight) Exercises list
sources.notes: Vertical-push / deltoid category list (overhead presses, raises) with per-exercise muscle role classification. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Hip (weight) Exercises list
sources.notes: Hip-extension / hip-hinge category list (hip thrusts, deadlift variants, glute work) with muscle role data. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Thigh (weight) Exercises list
sources.notes: Squat/knee-extension and knee-flexion category list (squats, leg press, lunges, leg curls) linking to per-exercise prime-mover/stabilizer analyses. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Squat Analysis (kinesiology)
sources.notes: Kinesiological squat breakdown: joints, movements, prime movers, synergists, antagonist stabilizers (erectors, rectus abdominis, obliques). Exemplar squat-pattern analysis. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Bench Press Analyses (kinesiology)
sources.notes: Kinesiological bench-press (horizontal-push) breakdown: muscle roles, grip-width biomechanics, cited research. Exemplar horizontal-push analysis. Proprietary.

sources.title: ExRx.net — Deadlift Analysis (kinesiology)
sources.notes: Kinesiological deadlift (hip-hinge) breakdown: joints, movements, muscle roles (glutes, hamstrings, erectors, adductor magnus). Exemplar hinge analysis. Proprietary.

sources.title: Muscle & Strength — Exercise Video Database
sources.notes: Exercise DB filterable by target muscle, mechanics (compound/isolation), force type (push/pull/hinge), equipment, experience level; per-exercise target + secondary muscles + force type. Cross-check source. Proprietary.

sources.title: weighttraining.guide — Muscles activated by hip-hinge exercises
sources.notes: Movement-pattern page mapping hip-hinge to activated muscles (glutes, hamstrings, erectors, adductor magnus) with isolation-vs-compound classification by joint action. Pattern-taxonomy support. Proprietary.

sources.title: weighttraining.guide — Vertical pushing exercises (muscle activation)
sources.notes: Vertical-push pattern → target (anterior deltoid) + synergists (triceps, lateral deltoid). Pattern-taxonomy support. Proprietary.

sources.title: weighttraining.guide — Vertical pulling exercises (muscle activation)
sources.notes: Vertical-pull pattern → lats (target); traps, rear delts, biceps, mid/lower back (synergists); how grip changes activation. Pattern-taxonomy support. Proprietary.

sources.title: StrengthLog — The Four Basic Movements of Strength Training
sources.notes: Defines push/pull/hinge/squat patterns with the primary muscles each trains and representative exercises — concise movement-pattern-to-muscle map for the taxonomy. Proprietary.

sources.title: StrengthLog — Exercise Directory
sources.notes: Directory linking to per-exercise pages with target muscles, equipment, instructions; index for movement-pattern coverage. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — The Complete Hypertrophy Training Guide (Israetel)
sources.notes: RP/Israetel master framework for exercise selection: stimulus-to-fatigue ratio (SFR), volume landmarks, rep ranges, technique across all muscle groups. Anchors the SFR field. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Complete Chest Training Guide
sources.notes: Best chest exercises + technique (press angles, stretch emphasis, upper/mid regional bias), volume/frequency. Mover + regional_bias source for chest. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Maximizing Back Muscle Growth
sources.notes: Best back exercises + technique: vertical vs horizontal pulling balance, grip/stretch cues, volume. Mover + regional_bias source for back. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Quad Hypertrophy Training
sources.notes: Nine quad movements (squat, leg press, hack squat, leg extension) with ROM/depth cues and volume. Mover + SFR source for quads. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Complete Hamstring Training Guide
sources.notes: Best hamstring exercises (curls vs hip-hinge), straight-set rationale, fatigue considerations and technique. Mover + regional_bias for hamstrings. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Complete Glute Training Guide
sources.notes: Best glute exercises + technique; why targeted glute work beats squats/deadlifts alone, volume, categories. Mover source for the glute-vs-hamstring hip-extension call. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Calf Training Guide
sources.notes: Best calf exercises, stretch/ROM technique, volume/rep ranges for gastrocnemius (knee-straight) vs soleus (knee-bent plantarflexion). Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Dr. Mike's Bicep Training Guide
sources.notes: Bicep exercise categories (full ROM, supination, peak contraction, stretch, compound), volume, frequency, interaction with back training. Elbow-flexion mover source. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Triceps Hypertrophy
sources.notes: Best triceps exercises by head (overhead/long-head stretch emphasis), technique, volume landmarks. Source for long-head vs lateral regional_bias. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Front Delt Hypertrophy
sources.notes: Front-delt selection + technique, overlap with pressing volume, weekly sets. Deltoid-head mover source. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Side Delt Hypertrophy
sources.notes: Best side-delt (lateral raise) exercises + technique, volume for shoulder width. Medial-delt mover source (relevant to cable-cuff lateral grip-bypass). Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Complete Rear Delt Training Guide
sources.notes: Rear-delt selection + technique, contribution from back rows/closer grips, direct volume. Shoulder-horizontal-abduction mover source. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Forearm Training Guide
sources.notes: Best forearm/wrist flexor-extensor exercises, technique, volume for grip and forearm size. Grip-demand context. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Ab Hypertrophy
sources.notes: Best ab/core hypertrophy exercises + technique, weekly sets (16-20), loading. Anti-extension / anti-rotation core mover source. Proprietary.

sources.title: RP Strength — Forearm Training, Demystified
sources.notes: Israetel-team guide on forearm/grip anatomy and whether to train grip directly or bypass — context for the pinky/grip_demand constraint and grip-bypass rationale. Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — How to Select Exercises for Muscle Growth
sources.notes: Canonical Nuckols framework for choosing AND substituting exercises by target muscle, SFR, and resistance profile — the conceptual backbone for the substitution graph and the equivalence_score rubric. Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — The Complete Strength Training Guide
sources.notes: Nuckols master guide: exercise tiering (core/auxiliary/accessory), technique and programming for squat/bench/deadlift + accessories. Supports fixed_or_dynamic tagging. Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — Is Regional Hypertrophy Predictable?
sources.notes: Nuckols review of how exercise selection drives regional growth (incline vs flat bench, EMG vs longitudinal hypertrophy predictability). Core evidence framing for regional_bias confidence grading. Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — Are Compound Exercises Best for Hypertrophy?
sources.notes: Compound vs isolation selection; regional examples (skullcrusher vs bench triceps heads, leg press vs leg extension). Supports is_compound + substitution caveats. Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — Do Lengthened Partials Stimulate Stretch-Mediated Hypertrophy?
sources.notes: Evidence review on lengthened partials / stretch position in selection+technique; effect sizes vs full ROM. Underpins the 'loses lengthened-position load' substitution caveats (e.g. seated vs lying leg curl). Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — Could a Small Leg Extension Tweak Double Your Growth?
sources.notes: Technique tweak (hip/seat position on leg extension) affecting rectus femoris growth — practical execution + a leg-extension substitution caveat. Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — How to Squat: The Definitive Guide
sources.notes: In-depth squat technique: bar position, stance/grip width, depth, individual biomechanics. cues/rom_notes source for the squat pattern. Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — How to Deadlift: The Definitive Guide
sources.notes: In-depth conventional + sumo deadlift technique, setup, biomechanics, cues. cues/rom_notes + grip_demand context for the hinge pattern. Proprietary.

sources.title: Stronger by Science — Evidence-Based Guide to Grip Strength & Forearm Development
sources.notes: When grip is the limiting factor in pulling, forearm flexor anatomy, and rationale for grip-bypass tools (straps) vs training grip — core to grip_demand and the pinky bypass logic. Proprietary.

sources.title: Jeff Nippard — The Ultimate PULL Workout (Back, Biceps, Rear Delts)
sources.notes: Science-based pull selection + technique (chest-supported rows, pullovers, face pulls, stretch curls) with study rationale. Cross-check for pull-pattern mover lists; not sole authority. Proprietary.

sources.title: Jeff Nippard — The Ultimate PUSH Workout (Chest, Shoulders, Triceps)
sources.notes: Science-based push selection + technique (press angles, stretch emphasis, machine vs free weight) with rationale. Cross-check for push-pattern mover lists. Proprietary.

sources.title: Menno Henselmans — Exercise Selection (podcast/article)
sources.notes: Henselmans' framework of biomechanical/physiological factors predicting growth per exercise: EMG ~40% MVIC threshold, resistance profiles, stretch emphasis. SFR + equivalence_score reasoning. Proprietary.

sources.title: Menno Henselmans — Lat Prayers: The Perfect Exercise for the Lats
sources.notes: Lat biomechanics: shoulder extension vs adduction, regional leverage, moment arms determining which lat regions row vs pulldown biases. Directly addresses the lat row-vs-pulldown regional_bias dispute. Proprietary.

sources.title: Chris Beardsley — How Can Exercise Strength Curves Affect Hypertrophy?
sources.notes: Core mechanistic explainer: how an exercise's strength/resistance curve interacts with length-tension to bias which region is loaded. Foundation for resistance-profile substitution caveats. Proprietary (Medium).

sources.title: Chris Beardsley — When Is Training at Long Muscle Lengths Beneficial?
sources.notes: Long-muscle-length training + fascicle-length increases; why exercises loading the stretched position differ in regional stimulus. Supports RDL-stretch and incline-stretch caveats. Proprietary (Medium).

sources.title: Chris Beardsley — What Is the Principle of Neuromechanical Matching?
sources.notes: Neuromechanical matching: brain activates a region in proportion to its moment-arm leverage at each joint angle. Key mechanism behind disputed mover/regional-bias claims (lat regions, glute vs hamstring, pec heads). Proprietary (Medium).

sources.title: Chris Beardsley — Does Leverage Determine Muscle Force (and Does That Matter)?
sources.notes: Internal moment-arm length / leverage and whether it determines force and hypertrophy. Directly addresses moment-arm reasoning used to argue regional/mover bias. Proprietary (Medium).

sources.title: Chris Beardsley — What Determines Mechanical Tension During Strength Training?
sources.notes: Active vs passive tension across muscle lengths and how strength-curve position changes the tension a region experiences. Underpins regional-bias + stretch-position caveats. Proprietary (Medium).

sources.title: Chris Beardsley — What Is Stretch-Mediated Hypertrophy and How Does It Work?
sources.notes: Stretch-mediated hypertrophy mechanism (passive tension, fascicle lengthening) — why RDL (hamstrings at length) and incline press (pec at length) may bias stretched-position-loaded tissue. Proprietary (Medium).

sources.title: PeerJ — Biomechanical Implications of Muscle Hypertrophy/Atrophy: a Musculoskeletal Model (Beardsley & Contreras)
sources.notes: Open-access (CC-BY) model deriving the ACSA↔internal-moment-arm relationship (MA change ∝ arcsine of sqrt of ACSA change). Primary quantitative basis for Beardsley's leverage/neuromechanical-matching framework.

sources.title: Variations in Muscle Activation During Lat Dorsi Weight-Training Exercises (Sperandei et al.)
sources.notes: Primary EMG study comparing lat activation across pulldown variants (front vs behind-neck vs straight-arm). Evidence for the rows-vs-pulldown / grip-position lat-bias dispute. PMC OA.

sources.title: Gluteus Maximus, Biceps Femoris & Vastus Lateralis EMG in Back Squat vs Barbell Hip Thrust (Contreras et al., 2015)
sources.notes: Landmark primary EMG study reporting higher upper/lower GMax activation in hip thrust vs back squat. Core source for the hip-thrust-vs-squat glute-bias dispute. Human Kinetics (JAB) — paywalled publisher.

sources.title: Bret Contreras — Squats Versus Hip Thrusts Part I: EMG Activity
sources.notes: Author's practitioner breakdown of the squat-vs-hip-thrust EMG data + strength-curve (peak resistance at hip extension) rationale. Mechanistic companion to the primary study. Proprietary blog.

sources.title: Gluteus Maximus Activation During Common Strength & Hypertrophy Exercises: A Systematic Review (Neto et al., 2020)
sources.notes: OA systematic review ranking GMax %MVIC across step-ups, deadlifts, hip thrusts, lunges, squats. Authoritative synthesis for which exercises bias glutes. PMC OA.

sources.title: Electromyographic Activity in Deadlift Exercise and Its Variants: A Systematic Review (Martin-Fuentes et al., 2020)
sources.notes: OA systematic review of EMG across deadlift variants (conventional, sumo, RDL, stiff-leg) covering hamstring (biceps femoris/semitendinosus), glute, erector activation. Core for RDL hamstring-bias claims. PMC OA (PLOS ONE).

sources.title: EMG Analysis of Romanian, Step-Romanian and Stiff-Leg Deadlift
sources.notes: OA primary EMG study comparing RDL variants on hamstring vs erector activation. Directly addresses RDL hamstring-bias and stiff-leg vs Romanian distinctions. PMC OA.

sources.title: Effect of Five Bench Inclinations on EMG of Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid & Triceps (Rodriguez-Ridao et al., 2020)
sources.notes: OA primary EMG study isolating clavicular vs sternocostal pec activation across inclines (-15 to 45 deg), with 30-45 deg optimum. Central evidence for the incline-vs-flat clavicular-bias dispute. PMC OA.

sources.title: Effects of Horizontal and Incline Bench Press on Neuromuscular Adaptations in Untrained Young Men (Chaves et al., 2020)
sources.notes: OA training trial measuring regional pectoralis thickness (3 sites) + clavicular/sternal EMG after flat vs incline vs combined press. Hypertrophy-outcome (not just EMG) evidence on regional pec bias. PMC OA.

sources.title: Neuromuscular Repatterning of the Pectoralis Major During the Bench Press After 10-Week Targeted Training
sources.notes: OA intervention showing regional (clavicular vs sternocostal) excitation can shift with targeted training — evidence on whether pec-head bias is fixed by leverage or trainable. PMC OA.

sources.title: Non-Uniform Excitation of the Pectoralis Major During Flat and Inclined Bench Press (PubMed record)
sources.notes: Primary study on regional pec excitation across flat vs incline + acute CSA via panoramic ultrasound. PubMed abstract record only (full text not confirmed OA) → license unknown. Incline-vs-flat clavicular-bias dispute.

sources.title: Assessing and Treating Gluteus Maximus Weakness — A Clinical Commentary
sources.notes: OA clinical commentary on GMax function, synergistic dominance (hamstrings substituting in hip extension), and exercise selection for glute activation. Context for the glute-vs-hamstring hip-extension mover dispute. PMC OA.

sources.title: Does Varying Resistance Exercises Promote Superior Hypertrophy and Strength? A Systematic Review (Kassiano et al., 2022)
sources.notes: Systematic review on whether swapping/varying exercises changes hypertrophy & strength — the evidence base for whether a substitute is equivalent (informs equivalence_score). PubMed abstract; full text paywalled (JSCR).

sources.title: Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Adaptations to Systematically Varying Resistance Exercises (2024)
sources.notes: Primary study on systematically rotating/substituting exercises and its effect on hypertrophy/strength — informs how interchangeable equipment variations are. PubMed abstract; paywalled.

sources.title: Are Lifting Straps a Game Changer or an Overrated Tool? An Exploratory Review (IJSPP 2026)
sources.notes: Most recent narrative/exploratory review synthesizing the strap literature: when straps bypass grip, effect on volume/hypertrophy, research gaps — best single overview for the grip-bypass decision. Human Kinetics (IJSPP) — paywalled.

sources.title: Ergogenic Effects of Lifting Straps on Velocity, Grip Strength, RPE & Grip Security During the Deadlift
sources.notes: Primary study quantifying what straps do in the deadlift (velocity, grip security, RPE) — core evidence for choosing straps as a grip bypass on heavy hinge pulls. ScienceDirect abstract; paywalled (Elsevier).

sources.title: Impact of Lifting Straps on the Max-Reps-to-Failure / Velocity Relationship During the Prone Bench Pull
sources.notes: OA primary study showing how straps change reps-to-failure/velocity in a horizontal pull — data on whether straps shift the working stimulus when bypassing grip. PMC OA.

sources.title: The Effect of Lifting Straps on Deadlift Performance in Females
sources.notes: Primary study on straps + deadlift performance in female lifters — population-specific grip-bypass benefit (smaller hands / lower absolute grip strength). PubMed abstract; paywalled.

sources.title: Effects of Lifting Straps on Max Strength, Reps & Muscle Activation During Lat Pull-Down (Sports Biomechanics 2021)
sources.notes: Primary EMG/strength study showing straps do NOT improve lat-pulldown 1RM/reps/lat activation in trained men — key counter-evidence on when grip bypass does and does not matter. ResearchGate record; paywalled (Sports Biomechanics).

sources.title: Comparative Effects of Core Versus Forearm Training on Pull-Up Repetition Performance
sources.notes: OA primary study showing forearm/grip training delays grip fatigue and raises pull-up reps — evidence that grip is a limiting (bypass-candidate) factor in pulling. PMC OA.

sources.title: ISSA — Effective Alternatives to Your Favorite Gym Machines
sources.notes: Certifying-body guide mapping common machines (leg extension, lat pulldown, etc.) to free-weight/bodyweight substitutes — directly serves the no-machine-swap requirement (substitution edges). Proprietary.

sources.title: N1 Training — Free Weights vs Cables for Resistance Training
sources.notes: Resistance-profile reasoning (flat cable tension vs gravity-dependent free-weight curve) — how to match a substitute's loading profile when a machine/cable is unavailable. Feeds substitution caveats. Proprietary.

sources.title: The Muscle PhD — Exercise Variation
sources.notes: Mechanistic explainer on how angle/equipment/ROM variation creates distinct stimuli — biomechanical reasoning for selecting an equivalent substitute. Proprietary.

sources.title: StrengthMath — Deadlift Grip Strategy: Mixed vs Double-Overhand vs Hook (+ Straps)
sources.notes: Decision guide comparing all four grip options when grip limits the pull; cites Kapicioglu biceps-rupture data (24/24 ruptures on supinated/mixed side). Serves grip-bypass + injury-avoidance edges. Proprietary.

sources.title: Torokhtiy — Lifting Hooks vs Straps: The Complete Guide
sources.notes: Practitioner (Olympic medalist coach) comparison of hooks vs straps: weight limits, dynamic vs grinding lifts, setup friction — when each grip tool applies. Proprietary.

sources.title: Torokhtiy — Figure 8 Straps vs Normal Straps
sources.notes: Figure-8 vs lasso strap mechanics (load onto wrist/skeleton vs finger flexors), quick-release safety, over-head vs below-waist rule — completes the strap-type grip-bypass matrix. Proprietary.

sources.title: Starting Strength — Hook Grip vs Straps (Stef Bradford)
sources.notes: Coaching-authority article weighing hook grip vs straps for training grip vs bypassing it — the train-vs-bypass philosophy that frames the grip_demand constraint. Proprietary.
